Courage; determination.
ex: It must have taken some guts to speak in front of that audience.
She doesn't take any nonsense from anyone—she's got guts.

senses.d: Content, substance.

senses.d: The essential, core parts.
ex: He knew all about the guts of the business: how things actually get done.
The guts of this Rolex watch are rock-solid.

senses.d: One's innermost feelings.
ex: If you need someone to spill your guts out to, I'm here.

senses.d: The ring in the gambling game two-up in which the spinner operates; the centre.
The center of the field.
To eat greedily.
To show determination or courage (especially in the combination guts out).
ex: He gutsed out a 6-1 win.

From Middle English gut, gutte, gotte, from Old English gutt (usually in plural guttas (“guts, entrails”)), from Proto-Germanic *gut-, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewd- (“to pour”). Related to English gote (“drain”), Old English ġēotan (“to pour”). More at gote, yote. The verb is from Middle English gutten, gotten (“to gut”).

senses.d: The alimentary canal, especially the intestine.
The abdomen of a person, especially one that is enlarged.
ex: You've developed quite a beer gut since I last met you.

senses.d: The intestines of an animal used to make strings of a tennis racket or violin, etc.
A person's emotional, visceral self.
ex: I have a funny feeling in my gut.

senses.d: A class that is not demanding or challenging.
ex: You should take Intro Astronomy: it's a gut.

senses.d: A narrow channel, passage, or stream of water. (Compare gote.)
ex: the Gut of Canso
FRAE Team-Gut to Whitley, wi' coals black and brown, For the Amphitrite loaded, the keel had gyen down;

senses.d: The sac of silk taken from a silkworm when ready to spin its cocoon, for the purpose of drawing it out into a thread. When dry, it is exceedingly strong, and is used as the snood of a fishing line.
To eviscerate.
ex: Holonym: field dress
The fisherman guts the fish before cooking them.

senses.d: To remove or destroy the most important parts of.
ex: Fire gutted the building.
Congress gutted the welfare bill.

senses.d: To dishearten; to crush (the spirits of).
ex: They were gutted by the court's decision.
What's bothering me is that I'd felt more for him than I realized, and it guts me that it's over before it can really get going.

senses.d: Made of gut.
ex: a violin with gut strings

senses.d: Instinctive.
ex: gut reaction
